channel.title: AI News Digest
channel.description: Official AI product updates from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and GitHub

item.title: product_surface
item.description: The Compliance API local session endpoints now also return transcripts of Claude in Chrome sessions ( product_surface value claude_in_chrome ), in beta for Claude Enterprise organizations, with your existing Compliance Access Key and the read:compliance_user_data scope. See Sessions on users' machines.

item.title: Introducing the Life Sciences Verification Program
item.description: Anthropic is an AI safety and research company that's working to build reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems.

item.title: How workers are unlocking new ways of working
item.description: New OpenAI Economic Research shows how workers use AI beyond traditional roles and which new activities become recurring parts of their work.

item.title: Reimagining advertising with AI
item.description: Explore new AI-powered advertising experiences from OpenAI, including Sponsored Agents, tools for marketers, and integrations with HubSpot and Shopify.

item.title: Our framework for reporting model misalignment
item.description: OpenAI shares a framework for tracking, investigating, and disclosing model misalignment, alongside six reports of unexpected or concerning model behavior.

item.title: How to connect AI usage to business value
item.description: Learn how ChatGPT Work and Codex analytics help teams understand AI usage and spend, identify training needs, and connect adoption to business outcomes.

item.title: Helping older adults use AI in everyday life
item.description: OpenAI and AARP are bringing free, hands-on ChatGPT workshops to 1,000 older adults across 10 U.S. cities to build practical AI skills safely.

item.title: CodeMender updates (v0.8.0)
item.description: Feature CodeMender updates (v0.8.0) This release introduces updates to CodeMender: Gemini 3.8 Flash default: Gemini 3.8 Flash ( gemini-3.8-flash ) is now supported and enabled as the default model for CodeMender CLI sessions, delivering faster inference and improved reasoning. A one-time notice in the CLI informs users when the new default is active.

item.title: Copilot budget increase requests are generally available
item.description: Previously, when a member used all the Copilot AI credits available to them, they were blocked from Copilot features that consume credits. This release adds a flow for them to request more budget the moment they hit the limit.

item.title: Code scanning AI Scan no longer requires CodeQL default setup
item.description: You can now use AI Scan for pull requests to find security vulnerabilities, even when CodeQL default setup isn’t enabled on a repository. Previously, AI Scan for pull requests only ran on repositories where CodeQL default setup was configured.

item.title: Reinforcement learning fine-tuning in the Google Cloud console (Preview)
item.description: Feature Reinforcement learning fine-tuning in the Google Cloud console (Preview) You can create, monitor, and test reinforcement learning fine-tuning jobs for Gemini models in the Google Cloud console ( Preview ). From the Models > Tuning page, you can configure Python code or model-based reward functions, test reward logic against sample prompts before launching a job, track training and evaluation metrics in real time, and test tuned checkpoints in Agent Studio.

item.title: Introducing Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking
item.description: Introducing Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking

item.title: GitHub Copilot suggests custom properties definitions
item.description: GitHub Copilot can now suggest allowed values when you create a custom property for repositories in your organization. This feature is in public preview for GitHub Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise plans.

item.title: Perplexity trusts GPT-6 Astra with end-to-end systems
item.description: Perplexity uses Astra to write communications, change software, and monitor production systems, and checks in much less frequently than with earlier models.

item.title: DevFest is back
item.description: DevFest 2026 is back and here’s how you can connect with one of the more than 800 global events to build, secure, and scale in the agentic AI era.

item.title: Configure cost and quality in Copilot auto model selection
item.description: GitHub Copilot auto model selection now offers three tiers: efficiency, balance, and intelligence. Choose the tier that reflects how you want auto to weigh cost, quality, and response time for each prompt.

item.title: compact-2026-09-04
item.description: The Messages API can now compact a conversation on demand on the Claude API, in beta with the compact-2026-09-04 beta header. Send the top-level compaction parameter, and the API returns a signed compaction block that summarizes the messages you sent. On later requests, send that block first, in place of those messages. You choose when to compact, the request can run in the background, and you can keep recent turns word for word after the summary.

item.title: Rapidly scaling online storage to serve over 1 billion ChatGPT users
item.description: Learn how OpenAI evolved Habitat from a Python library into a globally distributed storage platform serving 1 billion ChatGPT users and 22M requests per second.

item.title: Cognition helps Devin test its own work with GPT‑6 Astra
item.description: GPT‑6 Astra improves Devin’s ability to test software and show that it works, with the goal of helping engineers review less code and ship more.

item.title: Auto-resolution and analysis updates in Copilot code review
item.description: Copilot code review now resolves its own comments once you address them and writes smart commit messages for you when you apply its code suggestions. Behind the scenes, Copilot now uses a broader set of shell tools to validate the code it reviews, and an ensemble of agents produce a more thorough review within the Lite effort level.

item.title: Now everyone can put data to work
item.description: Meet the Data agent in ChatGPT Work. Connect company data, uncover insights, and build interactive dashboards with AI using natural language.

item.title: Introducing the Agents API
item.description: Build and launch cloud agents with the Agents API, a managed service powered by the Codex harness for orchestration, long-running sessions, and tool use.

item.title: Build more natural voice experiences with GPT‑Live‑1 in the API
item.description: GPT‑Live‑1 brings natural, full-duplex voice conversations to the API, with stronger instruction following, custom voices, and telephony support.

item.title: Introducing ChatGPT for Financial Services
item.description: Introducing ChatGPT for Financial Services, combining built-in financial data and GPT-6 Astra for research, modeling, and client-ready materials.

item.title: Expanding AI access and cyber defense for federal, state, local, and tribal governments
item.description: OpenAI and GSA will offer eligible federal, state, local, and tribal governments $0 license fees, 50% off usage, and expanded cyber defense support.

item.title: GPT-Live 1
item.description: GPT-Live 1 is now generally available in the API. Build full-duplex voice conversations that can continue while a backend model or agent handles reasoning and tools.

item.title: MAI-Code-1-Flash deprecated
item.description: We have deprecated MAI-Code-1-Flash across all GitHub Copilot experiences (including Copilot Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions) today, September 10, 2026. Model Deprecation date Suggested alternative MAI-Code-1-Flash 2026-09-10 MAI-Code-1.1-Flash Please update your workflows and integrations to use a supported model.

item.title: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — September 7
item.description: This week, GitHub Copilot introduces Jira integration in Copilot app and adaptive model orchestration with Project HydraFusion in Copilot CLI. We also introduced new agent automation in Visual Studio Code and expanded enterprise controls for Copilot in JetBrains.

item.title: AI Scan for pull request APIs in public preview
item.description: You can now manage GitHub code scanning’s AI Scan for pull request enablement with REST API endpoints at the organization and repository levels. This public preview gives teams a programmatic way to roll out AI-powered security detections for pull requests across select repositories without manually configuring each setting in the GitHub UI.

item.title: ant
item.description: Version 1.32.0 of the ant CLI adds ant beta:sessions connect, which attaches your terminal to a Claude Managed Agents session. You can follow the session live, send messages, and allow or deny tool calls that are waiting for approval. Pass --web to serve the Claude Console's session viewer locally and open the session there instead. See Connect to a Managed Agents session from your terminal.

item.title: auto
item.description: Claude Managed Agents permission policies now include auto: the server evaluates each agent or MCP tool call and runs it, denies it, or pauses for your approval. agent.tool_use and agent.mcp_tool_use events report how each call was evaluated in an evaluation field alongside evaluated_permission. See Let the server evaluate each call with auto.

item.title: Paul Christiano joins OpenAI Foundation Board
item.description: Paul Christiano joins the OpenAI Foundation Board and its Safety and Security Committee, bringing experience in AI alignment, safety, and standards.

item.title: GPT-6 Astra: The next generation in intelligence for work
item.description: Meet GPT-6 Astra, OpenAI’s most capable model for business, with advanced reasoning, computer use, and stronger writing and design judgment.

item.title: The AI policy window is open. We need to act.
item.description: Chris Lehane argues that stronger AI capabilities require stronger safety evidence, shared standards, and durable policy action while the policy window remains open.

item.title: Computer Use and Shell sandboxes are generally available
item.description: Feature Computer Use and Shell sandboxes are generally available Computer Use and Shell sandboxes in Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform are now generally available (GA). This release also includes the following new features for Agent Platform sandboxes: Shell sandboxes: Run untrusted shell commands, install packages, and manipulate files in an isolated Linux container using direct API /exec calls. For more information, see the Shell sandbox quickstart.

item.title: Remediate Code Quality findings with agentic autofix
item.description: Agentic autofix is now available to help you burn down findings in your code quality backlog. You can select up to 25 standard findings on a page and assign the whole set to Copilot in one action.

item.title: Enterprise managed permissions for GitHub Copilot agent operations
item.description: If you administer GitHub Copilot Business or GitHub Copilot Enterprise, you can now centrally control which agent operations are blocked, require human approval, or can proceed without a prompt. Managed permissions cover shell commands, file reads and edits, and network domains.

item.title: Enterprise-managed sandbox in Copilot for JetBrains
item.description: This update brings support for enterprise-managed sandbox policies, cross-file cursor jumps for next edit suggestions, global project context in chat, enterprise policy diagnostics, and a new connection between terminal Copilot CLI sessions and JetBrains IDEs. It also improves model selection, the chat experience, and reliability across MCP servers and agent sessions.

item.title: The Work Now Within Reach
item.description: Explore how more capable, affordable AI can expand the work people and businesses can accomplish—and make growth more economical.

item.title: Funding grants for new research into AI and teen development
item.description: Apply now for OpenAI’s $5 million grant program supporting independent research on how generative AI affects teen development, well-being, and safety.

item.title: OpenAI expands initiatives to support journalism from classrooms to newsrooms
item.description: OpenAI is expanding support for journalism with tools, training, and partnerships for students, educators, journalists, and news organizations.

item.title: On the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem
item.description: We’re sharing an AI-generated solution to the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem, including a writeup and a formal proof in Lean.

item.title: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.5
item.description: ChatGPT Images 2.5 helps turn your ideas, sketches, and reference photos into more personalized, polished images that better reflect your ideas.

item.title: GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst, GPT Image 2.5 Flare
item.description: Released GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst and GPT Image 2.5 Flare for image generation and editing through the Image API and the Responses API image generation tool. Use Sunburst for workflows where editing precision matters most, or Flare for fast, high-quality everyday image generation.

item.title: Prompt Cache Diagnostics
item.description: Prompt Cache Diagnostics is now generally available in the Responses API for GPT-5.6 and later supported models. Compare cache reuse against a previous response, identify reasons for cache misses, and follow troubleshooting guidance to improve cache reuse.

item.title: trusted-access program
item.description: GPT-Rosalind ( gpt-rosalind-research ) is now generally available through the trusted-access program for approved internal life sciences research. Standard pricing is $5 per 1M input tokens, $0.50 per 1M cached input tokens, and $25 per 1M output tokens.

item.title: 1Password increases engineering productivity 21% with Codex
item.description: Engineers at 1Password use Codex to rapidly build new features and internal tools, reaching production-readiness while maintaining rigorous security policies.

item.title: New customer portal help.github.com
item.description: The support portal has been redesigned and moved to a new home at help.github.com. It brings support, docs, learning, community, and account resources together in one place with Copilot-powered search across all of them.

item.title: GitHub Enterprise Server 3.22 is now generally available
item.description: GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES) 3.22 is now available and introduces new capabilities across the platform. Here are a few highlights in the 3.22 release: Administrators can configure Copilot CLI to work with GHES for enterprises that operate in disconnected or air-gapped environments without connectivity to GitHub Cloud.

item.title: Supporting independent journalism in Ukraine
item.description: OpenAI, AIRPPU and WAN-IFRA launch an AI program to help Ukrainian news organizations strengthen innovation, resilience, and independent journalism.
